text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Monday.

GERMANY - Bunds and futures were slightly lower in lacklustre late dealings as the market remained stuck in ranges with few fresh fundamentals to influence dealings, traders said. The June Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 100.45, up 0.01 from Friday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts ended 10/32 higher after a quiet session as traders awaited a raft of U.S. data due this week and Thursday's British election. Buying interest was in evidence at the lows but it quickly evaporated as prices rose. Price movements were exaggerated in thin trade. The June long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 109-4/32, up 12/32 from Friday's settlement price.

FRANCE - Bond futures finished the MATIF session marginally firmer, with PIBOR higher too, both amid modest volumes and unswayed by the latest opinion polls, which reinforced a view of the centre-right coalition winning the May/June election, albeit with a reduced majority. The June bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 128.30, up 0.02 from Friday's settlement price.

ITALY - Bond futures were sharply higher in late afternoon as the market turned bullish helped by the stronger lira and comforting words by Treasury minister Ciampi on Italy meeting Europe's single currency criteria and that 1997 one-off budget measures would be replaced in later years by permanent ones. The June bond future on LIFFE was trading at 126.90 up 0.95 from Friday's settlement price.
UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries opened unchanged ahead of a mid-morning report on March single-family home sales and facing four key economic reports later this week.

The conclusion of the weekend G7 meeting had little impact on Treasuries, analysts said. The June Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 107-6/32, up 2/32 from Friday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 7.14 percent.

JAPAN - Key June Japanese government bond (JGB) futures ended the Tokyo session lower, pressured by selling from dealers who squared positions ahead of a Japanese national holiday on Tuesday, market sources said. Most investors were reluctant to trade actively before the holiday. In after hours trading the June future on LIFFE was trading at 125.38, up 0.17 from Friday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - The primary market saw Brazil launch its well-publicized parallel bond raising around $540 million equivalent -- the first such euro-linked offering for an emerging market borrower. The parallel bond structure means that the three tranches -- denominated in Austrian schillings, Dutch guilders and French francs -- will be redenominated to the euro after the single European currency is introduced, scheduled for January 1, 1999.
